questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the parallel component (the projection) instead of the perpendicular one.
Computed $\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}-\underset{\sim}{a}$ instead of $\underset{\sim}{a}-\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{b}}\underset{\sim}{a}$.
Subtracted the component products, $(2)(1)-(7)(3) = -19$, when finding the dot product.

questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the projection instead of subtracting it from the original vector.
Subtracted the original vector from the projection.
Used $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}=9$ instead of $10$, omitting the second component's square.

questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the parallel projection instead of the perpendicular component.
Subtracted the original vector from the projection.
Used $(7)(1)-(6)(2)=-5$ as the dot product instead of adding the products.

questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 8 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the projection instead of the perpendicular component.
Subtracted the original vector from the projection.
Used the dot product $10$ as the projection multiplier without dividing by $|\underset{\sim}{b}|^{2}=2$.

questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 9 \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the projection instead of subtracting it from the original vector.
Subtracted the original vector from the projection.
Used $(2)(4)-(9)(3)=-19$ as the dot product instead of adding the products.

questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} -5 \\ 9 \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{c} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the parallel projection instead of the perpendicular component.
Subtracted the original vector from the projection.
Used the dot product $4$ as the projection multiplier without dividing by $|\underset{\sim}{c}|^{2}=2$.

questions.question_text:
The angle between $\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\underset{\sim}{b}$ is $120^{\circ}$ and $|\underset{\sim}{a}| = 20$.
Find the exact magnitude of the component of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b}$.

options.why: Used $20|\cos120^{\circ}|=10$, the parallel component's magnitude, instead of the perpendicular component's magnitude.
Treated the obtuse angle as making the answer negative; a magnitude is never negative.
Used $\sin 120^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}$ instead of $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

questions.question_text: Find the component of $\underset{\sim}{a} = \begin{pmatrix} \frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{7}{2} \end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{b} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$.

options.why: Gave the parallel projection instead of the perpendicular component.
Subtracted the original vector from the projection.
Used $9-(-\frac{7}{2})=\frac{25}{2}$ as the dot product instead of $9+(-\frac{7}{2})=\frac{11}{2}$.
